units.zh: 劉守光，深州樂壽人也。
units.en: Liu Shouguang was a native of Leshou in Shenzhou.
units.literal: Liu Shouguang was a man of Leshou in Shenzhou.

units.zh: 其父仁恭，初隨父晟客於范陽，晟以軍吏補新興鎮將，事節度使李可舉。
units.en: His father Liu Rengong had first accompanied his own father Liu Sheng as a dependent in Fanyang. Sheng was promoted from the clerical ranks to commandant of Xinxing Town and served under Military Governor Li Keju.
units.literal: His father Rengong had at first followed his father Sheng as a guest in Fanyang. Sheng was appointed commandant of Xinxing Town from the army clerks and served Military Governor Li Keju.

units.zh: 仁恭幼多智機，數陳力於軍中。
units.en: Rengong had been clever and resourceful since boyhood and repeatedly proved his worth in the ranks.
units.literal: Rengong from youth was very clever and resourceful and repeatedly displayed his abilities in the army.

units.zh: 李全忠之攻易、定也，別將于晏圍易州，累月不能拔，仁恭穴地道以陷之，軍中號曰「劉窟頭」，稍遷裨校。
units.en: When Li Quanzhong attacked Yi and Ding, the subordinate general Yu Yan besieged Yizhou for months without success. Rengong undermined the walls by tunnel and was nicknamed "Liu Tunnel-Head" in the army; he was eventually promoted to assistant commander.
units.literal: When Li Quanzhong attacked Yi and Ding, the subordinate general Yu Yan besieged Yizhou and for months could not take it. Rengong dug a tunnel to undermine the city; the army called him "Liu the Tunnel-Head," and he was gradually promoted to assistant commander.

units.zh: 仁恭誌大氣豪，自言嘗夢大佛幡出於指端，或云年四十九當領旄節。
units.en: Rengong was ambitious and high-spirited. He claimed to have dreamed that a great Buddhist banner sprang from his fingertips, and some said that at forty-nine he would receive a military governor's commission.
units.literal: Rengong was ambitious and bold in spirit. He said he had once dreamed that a great Buddhist banner issued from his fingertips, or that some said at age forty-nine he would receive the command baton.

units.zh: 此言頗泄，燕帥李匡威惡之，不欲令典軍，改為府掾，出為景城令。
units.en: Word of this spread. Yan commander Li Kuangwei took a dislike to him and refused to let him command troops, transferring him to a staff post and then sending him out as magistrate of Jingcheng.
units.literal: This remark leaked out somewhat. Yan commander Li Kuangwei hated him and did not wish him to command troops, so he was changed to a staff appointment and sent out as magistrate of Jingcheng.

units.zh: 屬瀛州軍亂，殺郡守，仁恭募白丁千人討平之，匡威壯其才，復使為帳中爪牙，令將兵戍蔚州。
units.en: When the Yingzhou garrison mutinied and killed the prefect, Rengong raised a thousand civilians, put down the revolt, and so impressed Kuangwei that he was again made a trusted retainer in headquarters and ordered to garrison Weizhou with troops.
units.literal: When the army of Yingzhou mutinied and killed the prefect, Rengong recruited a thousand commoners and pacified them. Kuangwei admired his talent, made him a close retainer in headquarters again, and ordered him to lead troops to garrison Weizhou.

units.zh: 兵士以過期不代，思歸流怨，會李匡儔奪兄位，戍軍擁仁恭為帥，欲攻幽州，比至居庸關，為府兵所敗，仁恭挈族奔於太原。
units.en: The troops, overdue for rotation and bitter at being kept in the field, were ripe for mutiny. When Li Kuangchou seized power from his brother, the garrison proclaimed Rengong commander and marched on Youzhou, but were beaten at Juyong Pass by the prefectural army. Rengong fled with his family to Taiyuan.
units.literal: The soldiers, because their tour was overdue and relief had not come, longed to return home and nursed grievances. When Li Kuangchou seized his elder brother's position, the garrison troops acclaimed Rengong as commander and intended to attack Youzhou. When they reached Juyong Pass they were defeated by the prefectural troops. Rengong fled with his clan to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 武皇遇之甚厚，賜田宅以處之，出為壽陽鎮將，從征吐渾。
units.en: The Prince of Jin received him with great favor, granted him fields and a house, appointed him commandant of Shouyang Town, and took him on campaign against the Tuyuhun.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin treated him very generously, granted fields and a residence, then sent him out as commandant of Shouyang Town and took him on campaign against the Tuyuhun.

units.zh: 仁恭數進畫於蓋寓，言幽州可圖之狀，願得步騎萬人，即指期可取，武皇從之。
units.en: Rengong repeatedly laid out plans to Gai Yu for taking Youzhou, asking for ten thousand foot and horse and promising a date by which he could deliver it. The Prince of Jin consented.
units.literal: Rengong several times presented plans to Gai Yu on how Youzhou could be taken, asking for ten thousand infantry and cavalry and promising he could seize it within a set period. The Prince of Jin agreed.

units.zh: 洎仁恭舉兵，屢不克捷。
units.en: Once Rengong took the field, however, he met defeat again and again.
units.literal: But once Rengong raised his army he repeatedly failed to win.

units.zh: 唐乾寧元年十一月，武皇親征匡儔。
units.en: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianning (894), the Prince of Jin led a personal campaign against Li Kuangchou.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianning of Tang, the Prince of Jin personally campaigned against Kuangchou.

units.zh: 十二月，破燕軍於威塞，進拔媯州，收居庸。
units.en: In the twelfth month he routed the Yan army at Weisai, took Guizhou, and recovered Juyong Pass.
units.literal: In the twelfth month he defeated Yan forces at Weisai, advanced to take Guizhou, and recovered Juyong.

units.zh: 二十六日，匡儔棄城而遁，武皇令李存審與仁恭入城撫勞，封府庫，即以仁恭為幽州節度使，留腹心燕留德等十餘人分典軍政，武皇乃還。
units.en: On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince sent Li Cunshen and Rengong into Youzhou to calm the populace and seal the treasury, then appointed Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to share civil and military duties before returning himself.
units.literal: On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince ordered Li Cunshen and Rengong to enter the city to reassure the people and seal the treasury. He then made Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving more than ten trusted men such as Yan Liude to administer military and civil affairs, and returned home.

units.zh: 二年七月，武皇討王行瑜，師於渭北，上章請授仁恭節鉞。
units.en: In the seventh month of the following year the Prince campaigned against Wang Xingyu north of the Wei River and memorialized the court to grant Rengong the command baton.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year the Prince attacked Wang Xingyu and encamped north of the Wei. He memorialized the throne requesting that Rengong be granted the command baton.

units.zh: 九月，天子以仁恭為檢校司空、幽州廬龍軍節度使。
units.en: In the ninth month the emperor appointed Rengong acting Minister of Works and military governor of the Lulong circuit at Youzhou.
units.literal: In September the Son of Heaven appointed Rengong acting Minister of Works and military governor of the Lulong circuit of Youzhou.

units.zh: 三年，羅宏信背盟，武皇遣李存信攻魏州，征兵於燕，仁恭托以契丹入寇，俟敵退聽命。
units.en: In the third year Luo Hongxin broke faith. The Prince sent Li Cunxin against Weizhou and called on Yan for troops, but Rengong pleaded Khitan invasion and said he would march only after the raiders withdrew.
units.literal: In the third year Luo Hongxin broke the alliance. The Prince sent Li Cunxin to attack Weizhou and levied troops from Yan. Rengong pleaded that the Khitans were invading and that he would obey orders once the enemy withdrew.

units.zh: 四年七月，武皇聞兗、鄆俱陷，復征兵於仁恭，數月之間，使車結轍，仁恭辭旨不遜。
units.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year, learning that Yanzhou and Yunzhou had both fallen, the Prince again demanded troops from Rengong. Envoys shuttled back and forth for months, but Rengong's answers grew ever more defiant.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, hearing that Yan and Yun had both fallen, the Prince again levied troops from Rengong. Within a few months messengers came in an unbroken stream, but Rengong's replies grew increasingly insolent.

units.zh: 武皇以書讓之，仁恭覽書嫚罵，拘其使人，晉之戍兵在燕者皆拘之，復以厚利誘晉之驍將，由是亡命者眾矣。
units.en: The Prince rebuked him by letter; Rengong read it and returned only abuse, seized the envoys, detained every Jin garrison soldier in Yan, and tempted Jin's best generals with rich rewards—so that defectors became numerous.
units.literal: The Prince reproached him in a letter; Rengong read it and showered abuse, detained his envoys, detained all Jin garrison troops in Yan, and again used rich rewards to entice Jin's fierce generals—hence many defected.

units.zh: 八月，武皇討仁恭。
units.en: In the eighth month the Prince marched against Rengong.
units.literal: In the eighth month the Prince campaigned against Rengong.

units.zh: 九月五日，次安塞軍。
units.en: On the fifth day of the ninth month he encamped at Anse Army.
units.literal: On the fifth of the ninth month he halted at Anse Army.

units.zh: 九日，渡木瓜澗，大為燕軍所敗，死傷大半。
units.en: On the ninth he crossed Mugua Stream and suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of the Yan army; more than half his force was killed or wounded.
units.literal: On the ninth he crossed Mugua Stream and was heavily defeated by Yan troops; more than half were killed or wounded.

units.zh: 既而仁恭告捷於梁祖，梁祖聞之喜，因表仁恭加平章事。
units.en: Rengong then reported victory to the Liang founder Zhu Wen, who was delighted and memorialized the court to make Rengong a Grand Councilor.
units.literal: Rengong then reported victory to the Liang founder, who was pleased and memorialized to have Rengong made Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 仁恭又遣使於武皇，自陳邊將擅興之罪，武皇以書報之。
units.en: Rengong also sent envoys to the Prince, blaming the war on unruly frontier commanders; the Prince replied in writing.
units.literal: Rengong also sent envoys to the Prince, claiming that frontier generals had acted on their own; the Prince answered by letter.

units.zh: 仁恭既絕於晉，恒懼討罰，募兵練眾，常無虛月。
units.en: Having broken with Jin, Rengong lived in constant fear of reprisal and recruited and drilled troops month after month without respite.
units.literal: Once Rengong had broken with Jin he constantly feared punitive action, recruited troops and drilled the masses month after month without pause.

units.zh: 光化元年三月，令其長子襲滄州，盧彥威委城而遁，遂兼有滄、景、德三郡，以守文為留後，請節鉞於朝。
units.en: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.
units.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua he ordered his eldest son to attack Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. He then held the three prefectures of Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and requested the command baton from court.

units.zh: 昭宗怒其擅興，不時與之。
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong, angered by this unauthorized aggression, withheld the commission.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was angry at this unauthorized campaign and did not promptly grant it.

units.zh: 會中使至范陽，仁恭私之曰：「旄節吾自有，但要長安本色耳，何以累章見阻？
units.en: When a court envoy reached Fanyang, Rengong told him privately, "I already hold the command in fact—I only need the proper insignia from Chang'an. Why should repeated memorials stand in my way?
units.literal: When a court messenger reached Fanyang, Rengong told him privately: "The command baton I already have myself—I only need the proper insignia from Chang'an. Why block me with repeated memorials?

units.zh: 為吾言之。」
units.en: Say as much for me there."
units.literal: Speak for me on this."

units.zh: 其悖戾如此。
units.en: Such was the arrogance and perversity of the man.
units.literal: His arrogance and perversity were such as this.

units.zh: 仁恭兵鋒益盛，每戰多捷，以為天贊，遂有吞噬河朔之志。
units.en: Rengong's armies grew ever stronger and he won battle after battle; taking this as Heaven's blessing, he set his sights on swallowing the whole Hebei region.
units.literal: Rengong's martial power grew ever stronger and he won victory in most battles; he took this as Heaven's favor and formed the ambition to swallow up the north of the Yellow River.

units.zh: 二年正月，仁恭率幽、滄步騎十萬，號三十萬，將兼並魏博、鎮定。
units.en: In the first month of the second year he led a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from You and Cang—claiming three hundred thousand—with the aim of annexing Weibo and Zhending.
units.literal: In the first month of the second year Rengong led a hundred thousand foot and horse from You and Cang, claiming three hundred thousand, intending to annex Weibo and Zhending.

units.zh: 師次貝州，一鼓而拔，無少長皆屠之，清水為之不流。
units.en: His army reached Beizhou and took it at the first assault, slaughtering every soul regardless of age until the Clearwater ran red and ceased to flow.
units.literal: His army halted at Beizhou and took it at the first assault, slaughtering every person without distinction of age; the clear water ceased to flow.

units.zh: 羅紹威求援於汴，汴將李思安、葛從周赴之，思安屯內黃。
units.en: Luo Shaowei appealed to Bian for aid; Liang generals Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou marched to his relief, and Si'an encamped at Neihuang.
units.literal: Luo Shaowei sought aid from Bian; Liang generals Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou went to help. Si'an encamped at Neihuang.

units.zh: 仁恭兵圍魏州，聞汴軍在內黃，戒其子守文曰：「李思安怯懦，汝之智勇，比之十倍，當先殄此鼠輩，次擄紹威。」
units.en: Rengong besieged Weizhou. Learning that Bian troops were at Neihuang, he told his son Shouwen, "Li Si'an is a coward; in wit and courage you are ten times his better. Destroy these vermin first, then take Shaowei prisoner."
units.literal: Rengong besieged Weizhou. Hearing that Bian troops were at Neihuang, he admonished his son Shouwen: "Li Si'an is cowardly—in wit and courage you are ten times his match. First destroy these rats, then capture Shaowei."

units.zh: 守文與單可及率漁陽精甲五萬，夾清水而上。
units.en: Shouwen and Shan Keji then led fifty thousand crack troops from Yuyang up the Clearwater.
units.literal: Shouwen and Shan Keji led fifty thousand elite troops from Yuyang up the Clearwater.

units.zh: 思安設伏於內黃清水之左，袁象先設伏於內黃清水之右。
units.en: Si'an posted an ambush on the left bank of the Clearwater at Neihuang, and Yuan Xiangxian another on the right.
units.literal: Si'an laid an ambush on the left bank of the Clearwater at Neihuang; Yuan Xiangxian laid an ambush on the right.

units.zh: 思安逆戰於繁陽城，偽不勝，徐退，燕人追躡，至於內黃，思安步兵成列，回擊之。
units.en: Si'an gave battle at Fanyang, feigning defeat and drawing back slowly. The Yan troops pursued to Neihuang, where Si'an's infantry formed line and wheeled to counterattack.
units.literal: Si'an met them in battle at Fanyang city, feigning defeat and slowly withdrawing. The Yan men pursued to Neihuang; Si'an's infantry formed ranks and wheeled to strike.

units.zh: 燕人將引退，左右伏兵發，燕軍大敗，臨陣斬單可及，守文單騎僅免，五萬之眾無生還者。
units.en: As the Yan were about to pull back, the ambushers on both flanks struck; the Yan army was shattered. Shan Keji was killed in the field; Shouwen alone escaped on horseback. Of fifty thousand men, not one returned alive.
units.literal: As the Yan were about to withdraw, the ambushers on both flanks sprang forth; the Yan army was utterly routed. Shan Keji was killed in the battle; Shouwen escaped alone on horseback. Of the fifty thousand, none returned alive.

units.zh: 時葛從周率邢、洺之眾入魏州，與賀德倫、李暉出擊賊營。
units.en: Meanwhile Ge Congzhou had entered Weizhou with troops from Xing and Ming and, with He Delun and Li Hui, struck the enemy camp.
units.literal: At that time Ge Congzhou had entered Weizhou at the head of troops from Xing and Ming, and with He Delun and Li Hui struck the rebel camp.

units.zh: 是夜，仁恭燒營遁走，汴人長驅追擊，自魏至長河數百里，僵屍蔽地，敗旗折戟，累累於路。
units.en: That night Rengong burned his camp and fled. The Liang pursued at full gallop from Wei to the Changhe—for hundreds of li the dead covered the earth, and broken banners and snapped halberds lay heaped along the road.
units.literal: That night Rengong burned his camp and fled. The Liang men pursued at full speed from Wei to the Changhe—for several hundred li the dead lay covering the ground; broken banners and snapped halberds littered the road.

units.zh: 鎮人又邀擊於東境，燕軍復敗。
units.en: Zhending forces ambushed them again on the eastern frontier, and the Yan army was beaten a second time.
units.literal: Zhen troops ambushed them again on the eastern border and the Yan army was defeated once more.

units.zh: 仁恭自是垂翅不振者累年。
units.en: From that day Rengong's wings were clipped, and for years he could not regain his strength.
units.literal: From then on Rengong's wings were clipped and he did not recover for years.

units.zh: 汴人乘勝攻滄州，仁恭率師援之，營於乾寧軍。
units.en: The Liang pressed their victory against Cangzhou; Rengong marched to relieve it and encamped at Qianning Army.
units.literal: The Liang took advantage of victory to attack Cangzhou. Rengong led troops to rescue and encamped at Qianning Army.

units.zh: 汴將氏叔琮逆戰，燕軍逗撓，退保瓦橋，乃卑辭厚禮乞師於晉，武皇遣兵逼邢、洺以應之。
units.en: Liang general Shi Shucong gave battle; the Yan army faltered, fell back to Wa Bridge, and then sent humble pleas and rich gifts begging Jin for aid. The Prince sent troops to threaten Xing and Ming in reply.
units.literal: Liang general Shi Shucong met them in battle; the Yan army hesitated and stalled, fell back to defend Wa Bridge, then sent humble words and rich gifts begging troops from Jin. The Prince sent forces to press Xing and Ming in response.

units.zh: 十月，汴人陷瀛、鄚二州，晉將周德威將兵出飛狐，仁恭復修好於晉。
units.en: In the tenth month the Liang took Ying and Mo; Jin general Zhou Dewei marched out through Flying Fox Pass, and Rengong renewed his alliance with Jin.
units.literal: In the tenth month the Liang took Ying and Mo; Jin general Zhou Dewei led troops out through Flying Fox Pass, and Rengong renewed friendly relations with Jin.

units.zh: 天祐三年七月，梁祖自將兵攻滄州，營於長蘆。
units.en: In the seventh month of the third year of Tianyou (906) the Liang founder Zhu Wen personally led troops against Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Tianyou the Liang founder personally led troops against Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu.

units.zh: 仁恭師徒屢喪，乃酷法盡發部內男子十五已上、七十已下，各自備兵糧以從軍，閭裏為之一空。
units.en: Having lost army after army, Rengong imposed harsh levies, drafting every man in his domain from fifteen to seventy, each to supply his own arms and rations for the campaign until the villages stood empty.
units.literal: Rengong had lost repeated armies; he imposed harsh laws drafting every man in the circuit aged fifteen and above through seventy, each to furnish his own arms and provisions for the campaign—the villages were emptied.

units.zh: 部內男子無貴踐，並黥其面，文曰「定霸都」，士人黥其臂，文曰「一心事主」。
units.en: Every man, high or low, had his face tattooed with the words "Establish the Hegemon's Capital"; scholars had their arms marked "Serve the lord with one heart."
units.literal: Every man without regard to rank had his face tattooed with the characters "Establish the Hegemon's Capital"; scholars had their arms tattooed with "Wholeheartedly serve the lord."

units.zh: 由是燕、薊人民例多黥涅，或伏竄而免。
units.en: Thereafter tattooing became common among the people of Yan and Ji, though some hid in the hills to escape it.
units.literal: Thereafter people of Yan and Ji were commonly tattooed, though some hid in concealment to escape.

units.zh: 仁恭閱眾，得二十萬，進至瓦橋，汴人深溝高壘以攻滄州，內外阻絕，仁恭不能合戰，城中大饑，人相篡啖，析骸而爨，丸土而食，轉死骨立者十之六七。
units.en: Rengong reviewed his forces and mustered two hundred thousand, advancing to Wa Bridge. The Liang dug deep trenches and high ramparts against Cangzhou, cutting it off inside and out so that Rengong could not relieve it. Inside the city famine was ghastly: men seized one another to eat, split bones for fuel, rolled earth into balls to swallow; six or seven in ten starved until only skin and bone remained.
units.literal: Rengong reviewed the hosts and mustered two hundred thousand, advancing to Wa Bridge. The Liang dug deep moats and raised high ramparts to attack Cangzhou; inside and outside were cut off and Rengong could not join battle. Inside the city famine was extreme—men seized one another to devour; they split bones to cook and rolled earth into balls to eat. Six or seven in ten died of starvation and left only bones.

units.zh: 自七月至十月，仁恭遣使求援於晉，前後百餘輩，武皇乃征兵於燕，仁恭遣都將李溥夏侯景、監軍張居翰、書記馬郁等，以兵三萬來會。
units.en: From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging Jin for aid. The Prince then called on Yan for troops; Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xiahou Jing, overseer Zhang Juhan, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join the campaign.
units.literal: From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging aid from Jin. The Prince then levied troops in Yan. Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xiahou Jing, overseer Zhang Juhan, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join him.

units.zh: 十二月，合晉師以攻潞州，降丁會，乃解滄州之圍。
units.en: In the twelfth month they joined Jin forces to attack Luzhou, won Ding Hui's surrender, and thereby lifted the siege of Cangzhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month they united with Jin forces to attack Luzhou, induced Ding Hui to surrender, and thus lifted the siege of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 是時，天子播遷，中原多故，仁恭嘯傲薊門，誌意盈滿，師道士王若訥，祈長生羽化之道。
units.en: The emperor was then driven from the capital and the central plains were in turmoil. Rengong swaggered at the Ji Gate, his ambition swollen to bursting. He took the Daoist Wang Ruone as teacher, seeking the path to long life and ascension as an immortal.
units.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was driven from the capital and the central plains were in turmoil. Rengong strutted at the Ji Gate, his ambition full to overflowing. He attended the Daoist Wang Ruone, seeking the Way of long life and ascension as an immortal.

units.zh: 幽州西有名山曰大安山，仁恭乃於其上盛飾館宇，僭擬宮掖，聚室女艷婦，窮極侈麗。
units.en: West of Youzhou stands the famous Da'an Mountain. Rengong lavishly built halls there in imitation of the imperial palace and gathered palace women and courtesans in the utmost luxury.
units.literal: West of Youzhou there is a famous mountain called Da'an Mountain. Rengong lavishly adorned pavilions there in imitation of the imperial palace and gathered young women and courtesans in extreme splendor.

units.zh: 又招聚緇黃，合仙丹，講求法要。
units.en: He also gathered monks and priests to compound immortal elixirs and study the essentials of the Way.
units.literal: He also gathered monks and priests to compound immortal elixirs and study the essentials of the law.

units.zh: 又以瑾泥作錢，令部內行使，盡斂銅錢於大安山巔，鑿穴以藏之，藏畢即殺匠石以滅其口。
units.en: He also minted coins of clay for circulation in his domain, seizing all copper cash to the summit of Da'an Mountain, boring caves to hoard it, and when the hoarding was done killing the workmen to silence them.
units.literal: He also made coins of clay for circulation in his domains, collecting all copper cash to the summit of Da'an Mountain, boring caves to store it; when storage was finished he killed the masons to seal their mouths.

units.zh: 又禁江表茶商，自擷山中草葉為茶，以邀厚利。
units.en: He also barred tea merchants from the lower Yangtze and picked mountain leaves himself to sell tea at great profit.
units.literal: He also forbade tea merchants from south of the Yangtze and picked mountain leaves himself to make tea for large profit.

units.zh: 改山名為大恩山。
units.en: He renamed the mountain Great Favor Mountain.
units.literal: He changed the mountain's name to Great Favor Mountain.

units.zh: 仁恭有嬖妾曰羅氏，美姿色，其子守光烝之，事泄，仁恭怒，笞守光，謫而不齒。
units.en: Rengong had a favorite concubine named Luo, a woman of striking beauty. His son Shouguang took her as mistress; when the affair came out Rengong flew into a rage, flogged Shouguang, and cast him out of his presence.
units.literal: Rengong had a favorite concubine named Luo, of lovely countenance. His son Shouguang took her as mistress; when this leaked out Rengong was furious, flogged Shouguang, and banished him from his table.

units.zh: 四年四月，汴將李思安以急兵攻幽州，營於石子河，仁恭在大安山，城中無備，守光自外帥兵來援，登城拒守。
units.en: In the fourth month of the fourth year Liang general Li Si'an struck Youzhou with a rapid column and encamped at Shizi River. Rengong was on Da'an Mountain and the city was unprepared; Shouguang led troops in from outside, mounted the walls, and held the defense.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year Liang general Li Si'an attacked Youzhou with a rapid force and encamped at Shizi River. Rengong was on Da'an Mountain; the city was unprepared. Shouguang led troops from outside to relieve it, mounted the walls, and held the defense.

units.zh: 汴軍既退，守光乃自為幽州節度，令其部將李小喜、元行欽將兵攻大安山。
units.en: After the Liang withdrew, Shouguang declared himself military governor of Youzhou and ordered his generals Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin to attack Da'an Mountain.
units.literal: Once the Liang army had withdrawn, Shouguang made himself military governor of Youzhou and ordered his generals Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin to lead troops against Da'an Mountain.

units.zh: 仁恭遣兵拒戰，為小喜所敗，乃擄仁恭歸幽州，囚於別室。
units.en: Rengong sent troops to resist but was beaten by Xiaoxi, who seized him and brought him back to Youzhou, where he was imprisoned in a side chamber.
units.literal: Rengong sent troops to resist but was defeated by Xiaoxi, who then seized Rengong and brought him back to Youzhou, imprisoning him in a separate chamber.

units.zh: 仁恭左右，迨至婢媵，與守光不協者畢誅之。
units.en: Everyone in Rengong's household, down to maids and concubines, who were not on good terms with Shouguang was put to death.
units.literal: All of Rengong's attendants, down to maids and concubines, who were at odds with Shouguang were put to death.

units.zh: 其兄守文在滄州，聞父被囚，聚兵大哭，諭之曰：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。
units.en: His elder brother Shouwen was at Cangzhou. Learning that their father was a prisoner, he gathered his troops and wept, telling them, "Alas, our parents—who bore us with such labor.
units.literal: His elder brother Shouwen was at Cangzhou. Hearing that their father was imprisoned, he gathered troops and wept aloud, addressing them: "Alas, alas, our parents—who bore us with such toil.

units.zh: 自古豈有讎父者，吾家生此梟獍，吾生不如死！」
units.en: Since antiquity has any son made war on his father? Our house has bred this monster; I would rather die than live on!"
units.literal: Since antiquity has there ever been one who made an enemy of his father? Our house has produced this owl and wolf-cub; I would rather die than live!"

units.zh: 即率滄、德之師討之。
units.en: He then led the armies of Cang and De against his brother.
units.literal: He then led the armies of Cang and De to campaign against him.

units.zh: 守光逆戰於雞蘇，為守文所敗。
units.en: Shouguang met him at Jisu and was defeated by Shouwen.
units.literal: Shouguang met him in battle at Jisu and was defeated by Shouwen.

units.zh: 既而守文詐悲，單馬立於陣場，泣諭於眾曰：「勿殺吾弟！」
units.en: Then Shouwen feigned grief, rode alone into the field, and weeping told his men, "Do not kill my brother!"
units.literal: Then Shouwen feigned grief, stood alone on horseback in the midst of the battle line, and weeping addressed the host: "Do not kill my younger brother!"

units.zh: 時守光驍將元行欽識之，被擒，滄兵失帥自潰。
units.en: Shouguang's fierce general Yuan Xingqin recognized him and seized him; the Cang troops, leaderless, broke and fled.
units.literal: At that time Shouguang's fierce general Yuan Xingqin recognized him and seized him; the Cang troops, losing their commander, broke and fled of themselves.

units.zh: 守光乃縶兄於別室，圍以叢棘，乘勝進攻滄州。
units.en: Shouguang then bound his brother in a side chamber, penned him in with thorn hedges, and pressing his advantage marched on Cangzhou.
units.literal: Shouguang then bound his brother in a separate chamber, fenced him about with thorn hedges, and pressing his victory advanced to attack Cangzhou.

units.zh: 滄州賓佐孫鶴、呂兗已推守文子延祚為帥，守光攜守文於城下，攻圍累月。
units.en: Cangzhou aides Sun He and Lü Yan had already made Shouwen's son Yanzuo commander. Shouguang brought Shouwen before the walls and besieged the city for months on end.
units.literal: Cangzhou aides Sun He and Lü Yan had already installed Shouwen's son Yanzuo as commander. Shouguang brought Shouwen to the foot of the walls and besieged the city for months.

units.zh: 城中乏食，米斗直三萬，人首一級亦直十千，軍士食人，百姓食墐土，驢馬相遇，食其鬃尾，士人出入，多為強者屠殺。
units.en: Inside the city food ran out: a dou of rice cost thirty thousand cash, and a human head ten thousand. Soldiers ate human flesh; civilians ate plaster and earth. Donkeys and horses gnawed one another's manes and tails. Scholars venturing out were often butchered by the strong.
units.literal: Inside the city food was exhausted; a dou of rice cost thirty thousand, and a human head also ten thousand. Soldiers ate men; commoners ate plastered earth. When donkeys and horses met they ate one another's manes and tails. Scholars going in and out were for the most part slaughtered by the strong.

units.zh: 久之，延祚力窮，以城降於守光，守文尋亦遇害。
units.en: At length Yanzuo's strength gave out and he surrendered the city to Shouguang; Shouwen was soon killed.
units.literal: After a long time Yanzuo's strength was spent and he surrendered the city to Shouguang; Shouwen was soon afterward killed.

units.zh: 守光性本庸昧，以父兄失勢，謂天所助，淫虐滋甚。
units.en: Shouguang was by nature dull and foolish. Seeing his father and brother fall, he took it as Heaven's aid and grew ever more cruel and debauched.
units.literal: Shouguang was by nature dull and foolish. Because his father and brother had lost power he thought Heaven was aiding him, and his cruelty and debauchery grew ever worse.

units.zh: 每刑人必以鐵籠盛之，薪火四逼，又為鐵刷劀剔人面。
units.en: Whenever he punished someone he placed the victim in an iron cage with fire closing in on all sides, and used an iron brush to scrape the face raw.
units.literal: Whenever he punished a man he would place him in an iron cage with fires pressing in on all four sides, and also use an iron brush to scrape the man's face.

units.zh: 嘗衣赭黃袍，顧謂將吏曰：「當今海內四分五裂，吾欲南面以朝天下，諸君以為何如？」
units.en: Once he put on an ochre-yellow robe and asked his officers, "The realm is torn apart; I mean to face south and receive the homage of the empire—what do you think?"
units.literal: He once wore an ochre-yellow robe and, turning to his generals and officials, said: "Today the realm within the seas is split four and five ways. I wish to face south and receive the homage of all under Heaven—what do you gentlemen think?"

units.zh: 賓佐有孫鶴者，骨鯁方略之士也，率先對曰：「王西有並、汾之患，北有契丹之虞，乘時觀釁，專待薄人，彼若結黨連衡，侵我疆場，地形雖險，勢不可支，甲兵雖多，守恐不暇，縱能卻敵，未免生憂。
units.en: His aide Sun He, a man of backbone and strategic sense, answered first: "Your Highness faces trouble from Bing and Fen in the west and Khitan threat in the north. They watch for weakness and league against us. If they join forces and invade our borders, rugged terrain will not save us; however many troops we have, we may not even hold what we have. Even victory would leave us in peril.
units.literal: Among his aides was Sun He, a man of firm backbone and strategic talent, who was first to reply: "Your Highness has trouble from Bing and Fen in the west and Khitan menace in the north. They watch for openings and wait only for our weakness. If they league together and invade our borders, though the terrain is rugged the position cannot be held; though our armor and troops are many, we may not have leisure even to defend. Even if we can repel the enemy, worry will not be avoided.

units.zh: 王但撫士愛民，補兵完賦，義聲馳於天下，諸侯自然推戴。
units.en: Your Highness should comfort the troops, cherish the people, replenish the army, and restore the tax rolls—let your righteous name spread and the lords will acclaim you of themselves.
units.literal: Your Highness need only comfort the troops and love the people, replenish the army and complete the taxes—let righteous fame spread through the realm and the feudal lords will naturally acclaim you.

units.zh: 今若恃兵與險，未見良圖。」
units.en: To rely on troops and terrain alone is no sound plan."
units.literal: To rely now on troops and rugged terrain—I see no good plan in it."

units.zh: 守光不悅，及梁軍據深、冀，王镕乞師於守光，孫鶴勸守光出援軍以圖霸業，守光不從。
units.en: Shouguang took offense. When Liang forces held Shen and Ji, Wang Rong begged Shouguang for aid; Sun He urged him to march out and seize his chance at hegemony, but Shouguang refused.
units.literal: Shouguang was displeased. When Liang troops held Shen and Ji, Wang Rong begged Shouguang for troops. Sun He urged Shouguang to march out in relief to advance his hegemony; Shouguang would not listen.

units.zh: 及莊宗有柏鄉之捷，守光謀攻易、定，諷動鎮人，欲為河朔元帥。
units.en: After Emperor Zhuangzong's victory at Baixiang, Shouguang plotted to attack Yi and Ding, stirred up the men of Zhending, and sought to become commander-in-chief of Hebei.
units.literal: When the Emperor Zhuangzong won victory at Baixiang, Shouguang plotted to attack Yi and Ding, stirring up the Zhen men, intending to become commander-in-chief of Hebei.

units.zh: 莊宗乃與鎮州節度使王镕、易定節度使王處直、昭義節度使李嗣昭、振武節度使周德威、天德軍節度使宋瑤，同遣使奉冊，推守光為尚父，以稔其惡。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong then joined Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, Wang Chuzhi of Yiding, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, and Song Yao of Tiande in sending envoys to invest Shouguang as Imperial Father—a stratagem to ripen his folly.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong then, together with Wang Rong, military governor of Zhenzhou; Wang Chuzhi, military governor of Yiding; Li Sizhao, military governor of Zhaoyi; Zhou Dewei, military governor of Zhenwu; and Song Yao, military governor of Tiande Army, jointly sent envoys bearing a patent of investiture, acclaiming Shouguang as Imperial Father, to ripen his wickedness.

units.zh: 守光不悟，謂藩鎮畏己，仍以諸鎮狀送梁祖，言：「臣被晉王等推臣為尚父，堅辭不獲，又難推違。
units.en: Shouguang failed to see through the ruse and thought the governors feared him. He forwarded their petitions to the Liang founder, writing, "Your subject was pressed by the Prince of Jin and others to accept the title Imperial Father; I declined firmly but could not refuse without giving offense.
units.literal: Shouguang did not understand; he thought the military governors feared him. He still sent the petitions of the various circuits to the Liang founder, saying: "Your subject was pressed by the Prince of Jin and others to be Imperial Father; I firmly declined but could not prevail, and it was hard to refuse further.

units.zh: 臣竊料所宜，不如陛下與臣河北道都統，則並、鎮之叛，不足平殄矣。」
units.en: Your subject believes the better course is for Your Majesty to make me overall commander of Hebei—then the rebellions at Bing and Zhen would be easy to crush."
units.literal: Your subject ventures to judge what is fitting: it would be better if Your Majesty made your subject overall commander of the Hebei circuit—then the rebellions of Bing and Zhen would be nothing to pacify and destroy."

units.zh: 梁祖知其詐，優答之。
units.en: The Liang founder saw through the pretense and answered him graciously.
units.literal: The Liang founder knew this was deceit and answered him graciously.

units.zh: 仍命閣門使王瞳、供奉官史彥璋等使於燕，冊守光為河北道采訪使。
units.en: He also sent Palace Gate Commissioner Wang Tong, Palace Attendant Shi Yanzhang, and others to Yan to invest Shouguang as Hebei circuit investigation commissioner.
units.literal: He also ordered Palace Gate Commissioner Wang Tong, Palace Attendant Shi Yanzhang, and others as envoys to Yan to invest Shouguang as Hebei circuit investigation commissioner.

units.zh: 六月，梁使至，守光令所司定尚父采訪使儀註，所司取唐朝冊太尉禮以示之。
units.en: In the sixth month the Liang envoys arrived. Shouguang ordered the court to draw up protocol for the Imperial Father and investigation commissioner; the offices produced the Tang rites for investing a Grand Marshal.
units.literal: In the sixth month the Liang envoys arrived. Shouguang ordered the relevant offices to fix the protocol for the Imperial Father and investigation commissioner; the offices took the Tang rites for investing a Grand Marshal and showed them.

units.zh: 守光曰：「此儀註中何無郊天改元之事？」
units.en: Shouguang asked, "Why does this protocol include no sacrifice to Heaven or change of reign era?"
units.literal: Shouguang said: "Why is there in this protocol no matter of sacrificing to Heaven and changing the reign era?"

units.zh: 梁使曰：「尚父雖尊，猶是人臣。」
units.en: The Liang envoy replied, "The Imperial Father is exalted, but he remains a subject."
units.literal: The Liang envoy said: "Though the Imperial Father is exalted, he is still a subject."

units.zh: 守光怒，投於地，謂將吏曰：「方今天下鼎沸，英雄角逐。
units.en: Shouguang flung the document to the ground and told his officers, "The realm boils like a cauldron and heroes contend for mastery.
units.literal: Shouguang was angry and threw it to the ground, telling his generals and officials: "Today the realm seethes like a cauldron and heroes contend.

units.zh: 朱公創號於夷門，楊渭假名於淮海，王建自尊於巴蜀，茂貞矯制於岐陽，皆因茅土之封，自假帝王之制，然兵虛力寡，疆場多虞。
units.en: Lord Zhu took a title at Yimen; Yang Wei a false name on the Huai; Wang Jian exalted himself in Ba-Shu; Maozhen forged edicts at Qiyang—all on the strength of fief grants, each aping imperial rites—yet their forces were weak and their borders insecure.
units.literal: Lord Zhu founded a title at Yimen; Yang Wei took a false name at Huaihai; Wang Jian exalted himself in Ba-Shu; Maozhen forged edicts at Qiyang—all because of fief grants of earth, each usurping the institutions of emperor and king—yet their armies were hollow and their strength few, and their borders full of worry.

units.zh: 我大燕地方二千里，帶甲三十萬，東有魚鹽之饒，北有塞馬之利，我南面稱帝，誰如我何！
units.en: Great Yan commands two thousand li and three hundred thousand armored men. We have fish and salt in the east and frontier horses in the north. If I face south and declare myself emperor, who can stand against me!
units.literal: Our great Yan has territory of two thousand li and three hundred thousand armored men. In the east we have the wealth of fish and salt; in the north the advantage of frontier horses. If I face south and declare myself emperor, who can match me!

units.zh: 今為尚父，孰當帝者！
units.en: As Imperial Father, who is fit to be emperor but I!
units.literal: Now to be Imperial Father—who is fit to be emperor!

units.zh: 公等促具帝者之儀，予且為河朔天子。」
units.en: Prepare the rites of an emperor at once—I shall be Son of Heaven of Hebei."
units.literal: You gentlemen hurry to prepare the rites of an emperor—I shall for the moment be Son of Heaven of Hebei."

units.zh: 燕之將吏竊議，以為不可。
units.en: Yan's officers whispered among themselves that this could not be done.
units.literal: Yan's generals and officials whispered among themselves that this could not be done.

units.zh: 守光置斧锧於庭，令將佐曰：「今三方協贊，予難重違，擇日而帝矣。
units.en: Shouguang set axes and blocks in the courtyard and told his officers, "The three parties have acclaimed me together; I can hardly refuse again—a day will be chosen and I shall take the throne.
units.literal: Shouguang set axes and execution blocks in the courtyard and told his generals and aides: "Now the three parties jointly acclaim me; I can hardly refuse again—a day will be chosen and I shall be emperor.

units.zh: 從我者賞，橫議者誅。」
units.en: Follow me and be rewarded; speak out of turn and die."
units.literal: Those who follow me will be rewarded; those who speak out of turn will be executed."

units.zh: 孫鶴對曰：「滄州破敗，仆乃罪人，大王寬容，乃至今日，不敢阿旨，以誤家國，茍聽臣言，死且無侮。」
units.en: Sun He answered, "When Cangzhou fell I was the guilty one; the King in his mercy has spared me to this day. I dare not flatter you and ruin state and house. Hear me out, and I will die without regret."
units.literal: Sun He replied: "When Cangzhou was broken I was the guilty man; the Great King in his tolerance has brought me to this day. I dare not flatter your purpose and mislead state and house. If you would but heed my words, I would die without regret."

units.zh: 守光大怒，推之伏锧，令軍士割其肉生啖之。
units.en: Shouguang flew into a rage, forced him down before the block, and ordered the soldiers to cut his flesh and eat it raw.
units.literal: Shouguang was greatly enraged, pushed him down before the block, and ordered the soldiers to cut his flesh and eat it raw.

units.zh: 鶴大呼曰：「百日之外，必有急兵矣！」
units.en: He shouted, "Within a hundred days an enemy army will surely come!"
units.literal: He cried out loudly: "Beyond a hundred days there will surely be an urgent army!"

units.zh: 守光命窒其口，寸斬之，有識為之嗟惋。
units.en: Shouguang had his mouth gagged and cut him to pieces inch by inch; thoughtful men mourned him.
units.literal: Shouguang ordered his mouth stopped and had him cut to pieces inch by inch; men of discernment sighed and grieved for him.

units.zh: 乃悉召部內官吏，教習朝儀，邊人既非素習，舉措失容，相顧誚笑。
units.en: He then summoned every official in his domain to drill in court ritual. The frontier men were unpracticed; their deportment was awkward and they laughed at one another.
units.literal: He then summoned all officials within his domain to be taught court ritual. The frontier people were not practiced in this by nature; their movements were unseemly and they looked at one another and laughed.

units.zh: 八月十三日，守光僭號大燕皇帝，改年曰應天。
units.en: On the thirteenth of the eighth month Shouguang declared himself Emperor of Great Yan and adopted the era name Responding to Heaven.
units.literal: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month Shouguang usurped the title Emperor of Great Yan and changed the reign era to Responding to Heaven.

units.zh: 以梁使王瞳、判官齊涉為宰相，史彥璋為御史大夫。
units.en: He appointed Liang envoy Wang Tong and adjutant Qi She as grand councilors and Shi Yanzhang as censor-in-chief.
units.literal: He made Liang envoy Wang Tong and adjutant Qi She grand councilors, and Shi Yanzhang censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 偽冊之日，契丹陷平州。
units.en: On the day of his usurped enthronement the Khitans captured Pingzhou.
units.literal: On the day of the false investiture the Khitans took Pingzhou.

units.zh: 莊宗聞之大笑，監軍張承業曰：「惡不積不足以滅身，老氏所謂『將欲取之，必先與之』。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong laughed aloud when he heard. Overseer Zhang Chengye said, "Evil must pile high before it destroys a man—as Laozi said, 'To take, one must first give.'
units.literal: When the Emperor Zhuangzong heard this he laughed greatly. Overseer Zhang Chengye said: "Evil not accumulated is insufficient to destroy the person—what Laozi said, 'If you wish to take something, you must first give it.'

units.zh: 今守光狂蹶，請遣使省問，以觀其釁。」
units.en: Shouguang has gone mad with arrogance. Send an envoy to inquire of him and watch for his weakness."
units.literal: Now Shouguang is wildly perverse. I beg that an envoy be sent to inquire of him and observe his openings."

units.zh: 十月，莊宗令太原少尹李承勛往使。
units.en: In the tenth month Emperor Zhuangzong sent Li Chengxun of Taiyuan as envoy.
units.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Vice-Prefect of Taiyuan Li Chengxun to go as envoy.

units.zh: 承勛至，守光怒不稱臣，械之於獄。
units.en: Chengxun arrived, but Shouguang in a rage refused to acknowledge subjecthood and threw him in chains.
units.literal: When Chengxun arrived, Shouguang in anger refused to style himself subject and had him shackled in prison.

units.zh: 十二月，莊宗遣周德威出飛狐，會鎮、定之師以討之，德威攻圍歷年，屬郡皆下。
units.en: In the twelfth month Emperor Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei through Flying Fox Pass to join Zhen and Ding in the attack. Dewei besieged for a year until every subordinate prefecture had fallen.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Emperor Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei out through Flying Fox Pass to join the armies of Zhen and Ding in campaigning against him. Dewei besieged for a year and the subordinate prefectures all fell.

units.zh: 守光堅保幽州，求援於梁，北誘契丹，救終不至。
units.en: Shouguang clung to Youzhou, begged Liang for aid, and courted the Khitans in the north, but no rescue came.
units.literal: Shouguang held fast to Youzhou, begged aid from Liang, and enticed the Khitans in the north, but rescue never came.

units.zh: 十年十月，守光遣使持幣馬見德威乞降，又乘城呼曰：「予俟晉王至即出城。」
units.en: In the tenth month of the tenth year Shouguang sent envoys with gifts and horses to Dewei to sue for surrender and called from the walls, "I will open the gates when the Prince of Jin comes."
units.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year Shouguang sent envoys with gifts and horses to see Dewei and beg surrender, and also called from the walls: "I shall leave the city as soon as the Prince of Jin arrives."

units.zh: 十一月，莊宗親征。
units.en: In the eleventh month Emperor Zhuangzong led the campaign in person.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned in person.

units.zh: 二十三日，至幽州，單騎臨城，召守光曰：「丈夫成敗，須決所向，公將何如？」
units.en: On the twenty-third he reached Youzhou, rode alone to the walls, and called to Shouguang, "Success or failure must be chosen—what is your decision, sir?"
units.literal: On the twenty-third he reached Youzhou, rode alone to the walls, and summoned Shouguang: "A man's success or failure must be decided in one direction—what will you do, sir?"

units.zh: 守光曰：「某俎上肉耳！」
units.en: Shouguang said, "I am meat on the block!"
units.literal: Shouguang said: "I am but meat on the chopping block!"

units.zh: 莊宗湣之，折弓為盟，許其保全。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong pitied him, broke a bow to seal an oath, and promised his life.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong pitied him, broke a bow to seal an oath, and promised to spare him.

units.zh: 守光辭以他日，莊宗乃令諸軍攻之。
units.en: Shouguang asked for another day; the emperor then ordered a general assault.
units.literal: Shouguang pleaded for another day; the Emperor Zhuangzong then ordered the armies to attack.

units.zh: 二十四日，四面畢攻，莊宗登燕太子墓觀之。
units.en: On the twenty-fourth the assault closed on all sides. Emperor Zhuangzong watched from the tomb of the Yan crown prince.
units.literal: On the twenty-fourth the attack closed in on all four sides. The Emperor Zhuangzong mounted the tomb of the Yan crown prince to watch.

units.zh: 俄而數騎執仁恭並其孥來獻，檀州遊奕將李彥暉於燕樂縣獲守光，並妻李氏、祝氏，男繼珣、繼方、繼祚等來獻。
units.en: Soon horsemen brought in Rengong and his household. Tanzhou patrol commander Li Yanhui captured Shouguang at Yanle County with his wives Lady Li and Lady Zhu and sons Jixun, Jifang, and Jizuo.
units.literal: Soon several horsemen brought Rengong and his family in submission. Tanzhou patrol commander Li Yanhui captured Shouguang at Yanle County together with his wife Lady Li and Lady Zhu, and the sons Jixun, Jifang, and Jizuo, and brought them in.

units.zh: 初，守光城破後，攜其妻子將走關內依劉守奇，沿路寒瘡足踵，經日不食。
units.en: After the city fell Shouguang fled with his family toward the passes to seek Liu Shouqi. Frostbite ravaged his heels and he went days without food.
units.literal: At first, after the city fell, Shouguang took his wife and children intending to flee into the passes to rely on Liu Shouqi. Along the road frostbite afflicted his heels; for days he did not eat.

units.zh: 至燕樂縣，匿於坑谷，令妻祝氏乞食於田父張師造家，怪婦人異狀，詰之，遂俱擒焉。
units.en: At Yanle he hid in a ravine and sent Lady Zhu to beg food from a farmer named Zhang Shizao, who found her manner strange, questioned her, and seized them all.
units.literal: Reaching Yanle County he hid in a ravine and sent his wife Lady Zhu to beg food from the farmer Zhang Shizao. Zhang thought the woman's appearance strange and questioned her; they were all seized.

units.zh: 莊宗方宴府第，引仁恭、守光至席，父子號泣謝罪，莊宗慰撫之曰：「往事不復言。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was feasting at the prefectural seat and had Rengong and Shouguang brought before him. Father and son wept and begged forgiveness. The emperor said, "Let the past be past.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong was feasting in the prefectural residence and had Rengong and Shouguang brought to the table. Father and son wept and begged pardon. The Emperor Zhuangzong comforted them: "The past need not be spoken of again.

units.zh: 人誰無過，改之為貴。」
units.en: Who is without fault? To mend it is what matters."
units.literal: Who among men has no faults? To reform them is what is precious."

units.zh: 乃歸之傳舍。
units.en: He then sent them back to the guest quarters.
units.literal: He then returned them to the guest lodge.

units.zh: 是月己卯，晉人執守光及仁恭，露布表其罪，驅以班師。
units.en: On the day jimao that month the Jin seized Shouguang and Rengong, published their crimes, and marched them away with the army.
units.literal: That month on the day jimao the Jin men seized Shouguang and Rengong, published a bulletin of their crimes, and drove them along as the army withdrew.

units.zh: 十一年正月，至晉陽，仁恭父子荷校於露布之下，父母唾面罵守光曰：「逆賊，破家如是！」
units.en: In the first month of the eleventh year, at Jinyang, Rengong and his son wore the cangue under the victory bulletin. The parents spat in Shouguang's face and cried, "Rebel! Look what you have done to our house!"
units.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, reaching Jinyang, Rengong father and son wore the cangue beneath the victory bulletin. The parents spat in Shouguang's face and cursed: "Rebel! You have destroyed the house like this!"

units.zh: 守光俯首不顧。
units.en: Shouguang bowed his head and would not look up.
units.literal: Shouguang bowed his head and paid no heed.

units.zh: 自范陽至晉陽，涉千餘里，所在聚觀，呼守光為「劉黑子」，略無愧色。
units.en: From Fanyang to Jinyang, over a thousand li, crowds gathered at every stop and called him "Liu the Black One"; he showed little shame.
units.literal: From Fanyang to Jinyang, more than a thousand li, wherever they passed crowds gathered to watch and called Shouguang "Liu the Black One"; he showed scarcely any shame.

units.zh: 莊守以仁恭、守光徇於都城，即告南宮七廟，禮畢，守光與李小喜、鄭藏斐、劉延卿及其二妻皆伏誅。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong paraded Rengong and Shouguang through the capital, reported to the seven temples of the Southern Palace, and then executed Shouguang with Li Xiaoxi, Zheng Zangfei, Liu Yanqing, and his two wives.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong had Rengong and Shouguang paraded through the capital, then reported to the seven temples of the Southern Palace. When the rites were done, Shouguang, together with Li Xiaoxi, Zheng Zangfei, Liu Yanqing, and his two wives, were all executed.

units.zh: 李小喜者，本晉之小校，先奔於燕，守光以為愛將。
units.en: Li Xiaoxi had been a petty Jin officer who defected to Yan, where Shouguang favored him as a trusted general.
units.literal: Li Xiaoxi had originally been a petty officer of Jin and had earlier defected to Yan; Shouguang made him a favorite general.

units.zh: 守光雖兇淫出於天性，然而稔惡侈毒，抑亦小喜贊成。
units.en: Though Shouguang's cruelty sprang from his nature, his worst excesses were also urged on by Xiaoxi.
units.literal: Though Shouguang's cruelty and debauchery sprang from his nature, the ripening of wickedness and extravagant poison owed something also to Xiaoxi's encouragement.

units.zh: 守光將敗，前一日來降。
units.en: The day before Shouguang's fall, Xiaoxi surrendered.
units.literal: On the eve of Shouguang's defeat, Xiaoxi came over to surrender the day before.

units.zh: 守光將死，大呼曰：「臣之誤計，小喜熒惑故也，若罪人不死，臣必訴於地下。」
units.en: Facing death Shouguang cried, "My error was Xiaoxi's delusion! If the guilty one is not killed, I will plead against him below."
units.literal: When Shouguang was about to die he cried out loudly: "My mistaken plans were because Xiaoxi deluded me. If the guilty man is not put to death, I shall surely appeal in the underworld."

units.zh: 莊宗急召小喜至，令證辯。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong hurried Xiaoxi forward to answer.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong hurriedly summoned Xiaoxi and ordered him to testify.

units.zh: 小喜瞋目叱守光曰：「囚父殺兄，烝淫骨肉，亦我教耶！」
units.en: Xiaoxi glared and shouted, "Did I teach you to imprison your father, kill your brother, and debauch your kin?"
units.literal: Xiaoxi glared and shouted at Shouguang: "Imprisoning your father and killing your brother, debauching your own flesh and blood—did I teach you that!"

units.zh: 莊宗怒小喜失禮，先斬之。
units.en: Angered by Xiaoxi's insolence, the emperor beheaded him first.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong was angry at Xiaoxi's lack of decorum and beheaded him first.

units.zh: 守光慟哭曰：「王將定天下，臣精於騎，何不且留指使。」
units.en: Shouguang wept, "When you settle the realm, I am skilled in horsemanship—keep me to serve."
units.literal: Shouguang wept and said: "When the King is about to settle the realm, I am skilled in horsemanship—why not keep me to command for a time."

units.zh: 二妻讓之曰：「皇帝，事勢及此，生不如死！」
units.en: His two wives rebuked him: "Emperor, it has come to this—better to die!"
units.literal: His two wives reproached him: "Emperor, matters have come to this—life is worse than death!"

units.zh: 即延頸就戮。
units.en: They stretched their necks to the blade.
units.literal: They then stretched their necks to receive the blade.

units.zh: 守光猶哀訴不已。
units.en: Shouguang still wailed on.
units.literal: Shouguang still pleaded in grief without end.

units.zh: 既誅，命判官司馬揆備彗櫝祭叕，瘞於城西三里龍山下。
units.en: After the executions he had judicial officer Sima Kui prepare burial rites and inter them three li west of the city at Long Mountain.
units.literal: After the executions he ordered judicial officer Sima Kui to prepare the broom casket and burial rites and inter them three li west of the city at Long Mountain.

units.zh: 令副使盧汝弼、李存霸拘送仁恭至代州，於武皇靈前刺心血以祭，誅於雁門山下。
units.en: He sent Vice-Commissioner Lu Rubi and Li Cunba to escort Rengong to Daizhou, offer his heart's blood before the Prince of Jin's spirit tablet, and execute him below Yanmen Mountain.
units.literal: He ordered Vice-Commissioner Lu Rubi and Li Cunba to escort Rengong to Daizhou, pierce his heart's blood before the Prince of Jin's spirit tablet as sacrifice, and execute him below Yanmen Mountain.

units.zh: 自仁恭乾寧二年春入幽州，至天祐十年，父子相承，十九年而滅。
units.en: From Rengong's entry into Youzhou in the second year of Qianning to the tenth year of Tianyou, father and son held power nineteen years before extinction.
units.literal: From the spring of the second year of Qianning when Rengong entered Youzhou to the tenth year of Tianyou, father and son succeeded one another for nineteen years until extinction.

units.zh: 劉陟，即劉龑，初名陟。
units.en: Liu Zhi—that is, Liu Yan—had originally been named Zhi.
units.literal: Liu Zhi—that is, Liu Yan—was originally named Zhi.

units.zh: 其先彭城人，祖仁安，仕唐為潮州長史，因家嶺表。
units.en: His forebears were from Pengcheng. His grandfather Ren'an served Tang as long secretary of Chaozhou and settled the family in Lingnan.
units.literal: His ancestors were men of Pengcheng. His grandfather Ren'an served Tang as long secretary of Chaozhou and settled his family in Lingbiao.

units.zh: 父謙，素有才識。
units.en: His father Qian was gifted and perceptive.
units.literal: His father Qian was by nature talented and perceptive.

units.zh: 唐咸通中，宰相韋宙出鎮南海，謙時為牙校，職級甚卑，然氣貌殊常，宙以猶女妻之。
units.en: During Tang Xiantong, Chief Minister Wei Zhou governed the Southern Sea. Qian was a lowly guards officer, but his bearing was extraordinary; Zhou gave him his youngest daughter in marriage.
units.literal: In the Xiantong period of Tang, Chief Minister Wei Zhou went out to govern the Southern Sea. Qian was then a guards officer of very low rank, yet his bearing was extraordinary; Zhou gave him his youngest daughter in marriage.

units.zh: 妻以非其類，堅止之，宙曰：「此人非常流也，他日我子孫或可依之。」
units.en: His wife objected that he was not their sort, but Zhou said, "This man is no ordinary man. Our descendants may one day rely on him."
units.literal: The wife, thinking him not of her kind, firmly opposed it. Zhou said: "This man is no ordinary stream. In future my descendants may rely on him."

units.zh: 謙後果以軍功拜封州刺史兼賀水鎮使，甚有稱譽。
units.en: Qian later won military merit and was appointed prefect of Fengzhou and commandant of Hesui Town, earning high praise.
units.literal: Qian later indeed won military merit and was appointed prefect of Fengzhou and concurrently commandant of Hesui Town, winning considerable praise.

units.zh: 謙之長子曰隱，即韋氏女所生也，幼而奇特。
units.en: Qian's eldest son Yin was born of the Wei lady and was remarkable from childhood.
units.literal: Qian's eldest son was Yin, born of the Wei lady; from childhood he was remarkable.

units.zh: 及謙卒，賀水諸將有無賴者，幸變作亂，隱定計誅之。
units.en: When Qian died, ruffians among the Hesui generals tried to stir revolt; Yin devised their execution.
units.literal: When Qian died, some ruffians among the Hesui generals hoped to stir up trouble; Yin devised a plan and executed them.

units.zh: 連帥劉崇龜聞其才，署為右都校，復領賀水鎮，俄奏兼封州刺史，用法清肅，威望頗振。
units.en: Circuit commander Liu Chonggui heard of his talent, made him right guard commander and again commandant of Hesui, then memorialized him as prefect of Fengzhou as well; his rule was stern and his prestige strong.
units.literal: Circuit commander Liu Chonggui heard of his talent, appointed him right commander of the guard, and again put him in charge of Hesui Town. Soon he memorialized that he also hold Fengzhou; his administration was stern and his prestige considerable.

units.zh: 唐昭宗以嗣薛王知柔石門扈蹕功，授清海軍節度使。
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong rewarded the heir Prince of Xue Zhirou's service at Shimen by appointing Yin military governor of the Qinghai Army.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, because of the merit of the heir Prince of Xue Zhirou at the Shimen escort, appointed him military governor of the Qinghai Army.

units.zh: 詔下，有府之牙將盧琚、譚玘謀不稟朝命，隱舉部兵誅琚、玘以聞，知柔至，深德之，辟為行軍司馬，委以兵賦。
units.en: When the edict arrived, guard officers Lu Ju and Tan Qi plotted defiance. Yin raised troops, killed them, and reported it; Zhirou on arrival was deeply grateful, made him campaigning marshal, and entrusted him with troops and revenue.
units.literal: When the edict came down, prefectural guard officers Lu Ju and Tan Qi plotted not to obey the court order. Yin raised his troops, executed Ju and Qi, and reported it; when Zhirou arrived he was deeply grateful and made Yin campaigning marshal, entrusting him with troops and supplies.

units.zh: 唐昭宗命宰相徐彥若代知柔復署前職。
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong ordered Chief Minister Xu Yanruo to replace Zhirou and reappoint Yin to his former post.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong ordered Chief Minister Xu Yanruo to replace Zhirou and reappoint Yin to his former post.

units.zh: 彥若在鎮二年，臨薨，手表奏隱為兩使留後，昭宗未之許，命宰相崔遠為節度使。
units.en: Yanruo governed two years; dying, he memorialized that Yin be acting governor of both commissions. The emperor refused and named Chief Minister Cui Yuan governor.
units.literal: Yanruo was in the command two years; on his deathbed he memorialized by hand that Yin be acting governor of both commissions; the emperor did not approve and ordered Chief Minister Cui Yuan as military governor.

units.zh: 遠行及江陵，聞嶺表多盜，懼隱違詔，遲留不進，會遠復入相，乃詔以隱為留後，然久未即真。
units.en: Yuan reached Jiangling, heard of banditry in Lingnan, feared Yin would defy the edict, and lingered. When Yuan returned to office, Yin was made acting governor but long went unconfirmed.
units.literal: Yuan reached Jiangling, heard that bandits were numerous in Lingnan, feared Yin would defy the edict, and delayed without advancing. When Yuan returned to the chief ministry, an edict made Yin acting governor, but for long he was not confirmed.

units.zh: 及梁祖為元帥，隱遣使持重賂以求保薦，梁祖即表其事，遂降旄節。
units.en: When the Liang founder became commander-in-chief, Yin sent envoys with heavy gifts; the founder memorialized the court and the baton was granted.
units.literal: When the Liang founder became commander-in-chief, Yin sent envoys with heavy bribes seeking patronage; the Liang founder memorialized the matter and the command baton was granted.

units.zh: 梁開平初，恩寵殊厚，遷檢校太尉、兼侍中，封大彭郡王。
units.en: In Liang Kaiping's first year favor ran deep; he was promoted acting Grand Guardian and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, favor was exceptionally thick; he was promoted acting Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Prince of Dapeng.

units.zh: 梁祖郊禋，禮畢，加檢校太師、兼中書令，又命兼領安南都護，充清海、靜海兩軍節度使，進封南海王。
units.en: After the Liang founder's suburban sacrifice he was made acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, named Protector-General of Annan and military governor of Qinghai and Jinghai, and advanced to Prince of the Southern Sea.
units.literal: When the Liang founder performed the suburban sacrifice and the rites were done, he was further made acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, ordered also to hold the post of Protector-General of Annan and military governor of the Qinghai and Jinghai armies, and advanced to Prince of the Southern Sea.

units.zh: 開平四年三月卒。
units.en: In the third month of Kaiping's fourth year he died.
units.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Kaiping he died.

units.zh: 陟，隱之弟也，隱卒，代據其位。
units.en: Zhi was Yin's younger brother; when Yin died he took his place.
units.literal: Zhi was Yin's younger brother; when Yin died he succeeded to his position.

units.zh: 及梁末帝嗣位，務行姑息之政，乃盡以隱之官爵授陟。
units.en: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded and pursued indulgent rule, he transferred all Yin's offices and titles to Zhi.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded, pursuing a policy of indulgence, he transferred all of Yin's offices and titles to Zhi.

units.zh: 先是，邕州葉廣略、容州龐巨源，或自擅兵賦，數侵廣之西鄙，陟舉兵討之，邕、容皆敗，因附庸於陟。
units.en: Ye Guanglue of Yongzhou and Pang Juyuan of Rongzhou had each seized military revenue and raided Guang's west. Zhi campaigned against them; both were defeated and became vassals.
units.literal: Earlier, Ye Guanglue of Yongzhou and Pang Juyuan of Rongzhou had each monopolized military revenue and repeatedly raided Guang's western borders. Zhi raised troops to campaign against them; Yong and Rong were both defeated and became his vassals.

units.zh: 又，交州土豪曲承美亦專據其地，送款於梁，因正授旄鉞。
units.en: Jiaozhou magnate Qu Chenmei also held his ground, submitted to Liang, and received formal investiture.
units.literal: Also, the local magnate of Jiaozhou Qu Chenmei held his territory exclusively, sent submission to Liang, and was formally granted the command baton.

units.zh: 陟不平之，遣將李知順伐之，執承美以獻，陟自是盡有嶺表之地。
units.en: Zhi resented this, sent Li Zhishun against him, seized Chenmei, and thereafter held all of Lingnan.
units.literal: Zhi resented this and sent General Li Zhishun to attack him, seized Chenmei and presented him captive; from then on Zhi held all the Lingnan lands.

units.zh: 及聞錢镠冊封吳越王，陟恥稱南海之號，乃嘆曰：「中原多故，誰為真主，安能萬里梯航而事偽庭乎！」
units.en: Learning that Qian Liu was made Prince of Wuyue, Zhi scorned the title Southern Sea and sighed, "The heartland is in chaos—who is the true sovereign? Why should I sail ten thousand li to serve a false court?"
units.literal: When he heard that Qian Liu was enfeoffed Prince of Wuyue, Zhi was ashamed of the title Southern Sea and sighed: "The central plains are in turmoil—who is the true lord? How can I sail ten thousand li by ladder and ship to serve a false court!"

units.zh: 梁貞明三年八月，陟乃僭號於廣州，國號大漢，偽改元為乾亨。
units.en: In the eighth month of Liang Zhenming's third year Zhi usurped rule at Guangzhou as Great Han and adopted the era Qianheng.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenming of Liang, Zhi usurped a title at Guangzhou, state name Great Han, and falsely changed the era to Qianheng.

units.zh: 明年，僭行郊禮，赦其境內，及改名巖。
units.en: The next year he performed a false suburban rite, amnestied his realm, and changed his name to Yan.
units.literal: The next year he falsely performed the suburban sacrifice, amnestied his domain, and also changed his name to Yan.

units.zh: 陟僭位之後，廣聚南海珠璣，西通黔、蜀，得其珍玩，窮奢極侈，娛僭一方，與嶺北諸藩歲時交聘。
units.en: After usurping the throne he hoarded southern pearls and jade, traded west to Qian and Shu for luxuries, reveled in extravagance, and exchanged yearly embassies with the northern Lingnan governors.
units.literal: After his usurpation he amassed pearls and jade of the Southern Sea, opened trade west to Qian and Shu for curios, and indulged extravagance to the limit, entertaining himself as a usurper on one side while exchanging missions yearly with the northern Lingnan governors.

units.zh: 及聞莊宗平梁，遣偽宮苑使何詞來聘，稱「大漢國王致書上大唐皇帝」。
units.en: Hearing that Emperor Zhuangzong had conquered Liang, he sent He Ci with a letter reading "King of Great Han to the Great Tang Emperor."
units.literal: When he heard that Emperor Zhuangzong had pacified Liang, he sent false Palace Gardens Commissioner He Ci on a mission with the letter "King of Great Han to the Great Tang Emperor."

units.zh: 莊守召見於鄴宮，問南海事狀，且言本國已發使臣，大陳物貢，期今秋即至。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong received him at Ye, asked about the Southern Sea, and was told that a great tribute mission would arrive that autumn.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong received him at Ye Palace, asked about affairs of the Southern Sea, and was told that his kingdom had already sent envoys with great gifts, expected that autumn.

units.zh: 初，陟聞莊宗兵威甚盛，故令何詞來視虛實，時朝政已紊，莊宗亦不能以道制禦遠方，南海貢亦不至，自是與中國遂絕。
units.en: Zhi had sent He Ci to test Zhuangzong's strength; the court was already chaotic and Zhuangzong could not govern the far south—the tribute never came and ties with China were severed.
units.literal: At first Zhi had heard that Zhuangzong's military power was very great and therefore sent He Ci to observe the truth; the court was already disordered and Zhuangzong could not by principle control distant regions—the Southern Sea tribute never came, and from then on contact with China was cut off.

units.zh: 唐同光三年冬，白龍見於南海，改偽乾亨元年為白龍元年，陟又改名龔，以符龍之瑞也。
units.en: In Tongguang's third winter a white dragon appeared in the Southern Sea; he changed Qianheng to White Dragon and renamed himself Gong to match the omen.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year of Tongguang of Tang a white dragon appeared in the Southern Sea; he changed the false first year of Qianheng to the first year of White Dragon and again changed his name to Gong to match the dragon omen.

units.zh: 白龍四年春，又改大有元年。
units.en: In White Dragon's fourth spring he changed the era to Dayou.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of White Dragon he again changed to the first year of Dayou.

units.zh: 是歲，陟僭行耤田之禮。
units.en: That year he performed a false plowing rite.
units.literal: That year Zhi falsely performed the plowing rite.

units.zh: 陟之季年，有梵僧善占算之術，謂陟不利名龔，他年慮有此姓敗事，陟又改名纻。
units.en: Late in life a Buddhist monk said the name Gong was unlucky and that a man of that surname would ruin him; Zhi changed his name again to Zhu.
units.literal: In Zhi's later years a Buddhist monk skilled in divination said the name Gong was unlucky and that in future he feared someone of that surname would ruin matters; Zhi again changed his name to Zhu.

units.zh: 纻讀為儼，古文無此字，蓋妄撰也。
units.en: Zhu was read as Yan; the character did not exist in antiquity—it was invented.
units.literal: Zhu is read as Yan; there is no such character in ancient writing—it was simply fabricated.

units.zh: 陟性雖聰辯，然好行苛虐，至有炮烙、刳剔、截舌、灌鼻之刑，一方之民，若據爐炭。
units.en: Clever though he was, Zhi loved cruel punishments—branding, disemboweling, tongue-cutting, nose-pouring—so that his people lived over coals.
units.literal: Though clever and eloquent by nature, Zhi loved harsh cruelty, even employing branding-oven, disemboweling, tongue-cutting, and nose-pouring punishments; the people of his domain were as if over coals.

units.zh: 惟厚自奉養，廣務華靡，末年起玉堂珠殿，飾以金碧翠羽，嶺北行商或至其國，皆召而示之，誇其壯麗。
units.en: He pampered himself lavishly and in his last years built jade and pearl halls adorned with gold and kingfisher plumes, summoning northern merchants to boast of their splendor.
units.literal: He indulged only himself lavishly, pursued splendor widely, and in his later years raised halls of jade and pearl, adorned with gold, green, and kingfisher feathers. Merchants from north of the ranges who reached his state were summoned and shown these things to boast of their grandeur.

units.zh: 每對北人自言家本鹹秦，恥為蠻夷之主。
units.en: Facing northerners he claimed descent from Qin on the Wei and professed shame at ruling barbarians.
units.literal: Whenever he faced northerners he would say his family was originally from Qin on the Wei and was ashamed to be master of barbarians.

units.zh: 又呼中國帝王為洛州刺史，其妄自尊大，皆此類也。
units.en: He called China's emperor the prefect of Luozhou—such was his arrogant conceit.
units.literal: He also called the emperor of China the prefect of Luozhou—all his arrogant self-exaltation was of this kind.

units.zh: 晉天福七年夏四月，陟以疾卒，凡僭號二十六年，年五十四。
units.en: In the fourth month of Jin Tianfu's seventh year Zhi died of illness, having usurped for twenty-six years at age fifty-four.
units.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the seventh year of Tianfu of Jin, Zhi died of illness. He had usurped for twenty-six years and was fifty-four.

units.zh: 偽謚為天皇大帝，廟號高祖，陵曰康陵。
units.en: His false posthumous title was Great Heavenly Emperor, temple name High Ancestor, tomb Kangling.
units.literal: His false posthumous title was Great Heavenly Emperor, temple name Gaozu, tomb name Kangling.

units.zh: 子玢嗣。
units.en: His son Bin succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Bin succeeded.

units.zh: 玢，陟長子也。
units.en: Bin was Zhi's eldest son.
units.literal: Bin was Zhi's eldest son.

units.zh: 初封賓王，又封秦王。
units.en: He was first made Prince of Bin, then Prince of Qin.
units.literal: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Bin, then again Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 陟卒，遂襲位，偽號光天。
units.en: When Zhi died he succeeded and adopted the false reign title Radiant Heaven.
units.literal: When Zhi died he succeeded to the position and took the false reign title Guangtian.

units.zh: 玢性庸昧，僭位之後，大恣荒淫。
units.en: Dull and ignorant by nature, after usurping the throne Bin gave himself over to debauchery.
units.literal: Bin was dull and ignorant by nature; after usurping the throne he indulged heavily in debauchery.

units.zh: 尋為其弟晟等所弒，在位一年，偽謚為殤帝。
units.en: Soon his younger brother Sheng and others assassinated him. He reigned one year and received the false posthumous title Emperor Shang.
units.literal: Soon he was assassinated by his younger brother Sheng and others. He reigned one year and was given the false posthumous title Emperor Shang.

units.zh: 晟，陟第二子也。
units.en: Sheng was Zhi's second son.
units.literal: Sheng was Zhi's second son.

units.zh: 偽封勤王，又封晉王。
units.en: He was falsely made Diligent King and then Prince of Jin.
units.literal: He was falsely enfeoffed Diligent King and again Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 玢之立也，多行淫虐，人皆患之，晟因與其弟偽越王昌等同謀弒玢，自立為帝，改元為應乾，又改為乾和。
units.en: When Bin succeeded he debauched and tyrannized until all resented him. Sheng joined his brother the false Prince of Yue Chang to murder Bin, made himself emperor, adopted Responding to Qian, then Qianhe.
units.literal: When Bin succeeded he practiced much debauchery and cruelty and all men resented him. Sheng joined his brother the false Prince of Yue Chang and others in a plot to assassinate Bin, made himself emperor, changed the era to Responding to Qian, then again to Qianhe.

units.zh: 晟率性荒暴，得志之後，專以威刑禦下，多誅滅舊臣及其昆仲，數年之間，宗族殆盡。
units.en: Reckless and violent by nature, once enthroned Sheng ruled by terror, slaughtering old ministers and kinsmen until the clan was nearly gone within years.
units.literal: Sheng was by nature reckless and violent; once he had his wish he governed subordinates solely by harsh punishment, executing many old ministers and their brothers; within a few years the clan was nearly exterminated.

units.zh: 又造生地獄，凡湯鑊、鐵床之類，無不備焉。
units.en: He built a hell on earth, complete with boiling cauldrons and iron beds.
units.literal: He also built a hell on earth, with boiling cauldrons, iron beds, and the like all complete.

units.zh: 人有小過，咸被其苦。
units.en: Even small faults brought these torments.
units.literal: Whoever committed a small fault was made to suffer them.

units.zh: 及湖南馬氏昆弟尋戈，晟因其釁，遣兵攻桂林管內諸郡及郴、連、梧、賀等州，皆克之，自此全有南越之地。
units.en: When the Ma brothers of Hunan fell out, Sheng attacked Guilin's prefectures and Chen, Lian, Wu, and He, taking them all and holding the whole Southern Yue.
units.literal: When the Ma brothers of Hunan fought among themselves, Sheng seized the opening and sent troops to attack the prefectures within Guilin command and Chen, Lian, Wu, and He—all were taken; from then on he held all the lands of the Southern Yue.

units.zh: 周顯德五年秋八月，晟以疾卒，偽謚曰文武光聖明孝皇帝，廟號中宗，陵曰昭陵。
units.en: In the eighth month of Zhou Xiande's fifth year Sheng died. His false posthumous title was Civil and Martial, Radiant and Sagely, Bright and Filial Emperor; temple name Middle Ancestor; tomb Zhaoling.
units.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, Sheng died of illness. His false posthumous title was Civil and Martial, Radiant and Sagely, Bright and Filial Emperor; temple name Middle Ancestor; tomb Zhaoling.

units.zh: 是歲，晟以六月望夜宴於甘泉宮，是夕月有食之，測在牛女之度，晟自覽占書，既而投之於地，曰：「自古豈有長存者乎！」
units.en: That year on the mid-autumn full moon he feasted at Sweet Spring Palace. An eclipse fell in the Ox and Woman mansions. Sheng read the prognostic books, flung them down, and said, "Since antiquity has anyone lived forever?"
units.literal: That year, on the night of the mid-autumn full moon Sheng feasted at Sweet Spring Palace. That night the moon was eclipsed, calculated in the degrees of Ox and Woman. Sheng himself looked at prognostic books, then threw them to the ground and said: "Since antiquity has anyone endured forever!"

units.zh: 縱長夜之飲，至是而卒。
units.en: He drank through the long night and died.
units.literal: He gave himself to drinking through the long night and died then.

units.zh: 鋹，晟長子也。
units.en: Chang was Sheng's eldest son.
units.literal: Chang was Sheng's eldest son.

units.zh: 偽封衛王。
units.en: He was falsely made Prince of Wei.
units.literal: He was falsely enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 晟卒，乃襲偽位，時年十七，改元為大寶。
units.en: When Sheng died he usurped the throne at seventeen and adopted the era Great Treasure.
units.literal: When Sheng died he usurped the throne at age seventeen and changed the era to Great Treasure.

units.zh: 鋹性庸懦，不能治其國，政事鹹委於閹官，復有宮人具冠帶、預職官、理外事者，由是綱紀大壞。
units.en: Timid and incompetent, Chang entrusted government to eunuchs; palace women wore official dress, held nominal posts, and handled state affairs until discipline collapsed entirely.
units.literal: Chang was by nature timid and weak and could not govern his state; affairs were all entrusted to eunuchs, and palace women also wore caps and belts, held nominal offices, and handled external affairs—so that government discipline was utterly ruined.

units.zh: 先是，廣州法性寺有菩提樹一株，高一百四十尺，大十圍，傳云蕭梁時西域僧真諦之所手植，蓋四百餘年矣，皇朝乾德五年夏，為大風所拔。
units.en: Earlier at Guangzhou's Faxi Temple stood a bodhi tree one hundred forty chi tall and ten arm-spans around, said to have been planted by the Western monk Paramartha in the Liang dynasty over four hundred years before. In the summer of Our Dynasty's fifth year of Qiande a great wind uprooted it.
units.literal: Earlier, at the Faxi Temple in Guangzhou there was one bodhi tree, one hundred forty chi high and ten arm-spans around the trunk. Tradition says it was planted by hand by the Western Regions monk Paramartha in the Liang of Xiao, more than four hundred years ago. In the summer of the fifth year of Qiande of Our Dynasty it was uprooted by a great wind.

units.zh: 是歲秋，鋹之寢室屢為雷震，識者知其必亡。
units.en: That autumn thunder struck Chang's bedchamber again and again; the knowing said he was doomed.
units.literal: That autumn Chang's sleeping chamber was repeatedly struck by thunder; men of discernment knew he would surely perish.

units.zh: 皇朝開寶三年夏，王師始議南征。
units.en: In the summer of Kaibao's third year the imperial army began planning the southern expedition.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year of Kaibao of Our Dynasty the imperial army first deliberated a southern campaign.

units.zh: 四年二月五日，王師壓廣州，鋹盡焚其府庫，將赴火而死，既而不能引決，尋為王師所擒，舉族遷於京師。
units.en: On the fifth of the second month of the fourth year the imperial army reached Guangzhou. Chang burned the treasury and meant to die in the fire but could not; he was seized and his clan was sent to the capital.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the second month of the fourth year the imperial army pressed Guangzhou. Chang burned all the treasury stores and intended to die in the flames, yet could not bring himself to it; soon he was seized by the imperial army and his whole clan was moved to the capital.

units.zh: 皇上赦而不誅，仍賜爵為恩赦侯，其後事具皇家日曆。
units.en: The emperor spared him and granted the title Marquis of Enpardon; his later fate is recorded in the imperial calendar.
units.literal: The emperor pardoned him without execution and still granted the title Marquis of Enpardon; his later affairs are fully recorded in the imperial calendar.

units.zh: 陟始自梁貞明三年僭號，歷三世四主，至皇朝開寶四年，凡五十五年而亡。
units.en: From Zhi's usurpation in Liang Zhenming's third year through three generations and four rulers until Kaibao's fourth year, the regime lasted fifty-five years.
units.literal: From Zhi's first usurpation in the third year of Zhenming of Liang through three generations and four rulers, until the fourth year of Kaibao of Our Dynasty, fifty-five years in all passed before extinction.

units.zh: 劉崇，太原人，漢高祖之從弟也。
units.en: Liu Chong was from Taiyuan, a younger cousin of the Han founder.
units.literal: Liu Chong was a man of Taiyuan, a younger cousin of the Founder of Han.

units.zh: 少無賴，好陸博意錢之戲，弱冠隸河東軍。
units.en: As a youth he was a ruffian who loved dice and gambling; at twenty he joined the Hedong army.
units.literal: In youth he was a ruffian, fond of gambling games with dice and stake-money; at twenty he entered the Hedong army.

units.zh: 唐長興中，遷虢州軍校。
units.en: In Tang Changxing he was made army commander of Guozhou.
units.literal: In the Changxing period of Tang he was promoted to army commander of Guozhou.

units.zh: 漢祖鎮並、汾，奏為河東步軍都指揮使。
units.en: When the Han founder held Bing and Fen he had Chong appointed overall commander of Hedong infantry.
units.literal: When the Han founder governed Bing and Fen he memorialized that Chong be made overall commander of Hedong infantry.

units.zh: 逾年，授麟州刺史，復為河東馬步軍都指揮使兼三城巡檢使，遙領泗州防禦使。
units.en: A year later he was made prefect of Lin, again overall commander of Hedong horse and foot and inspector of the Three Cities, and nominally Defender of Sizhou.
units.literal: After a year he was appointed prefect of Linzhou, again made overall commander of Hedong horse and foot and concurrently inspector of the Three Cities, and held the post of Defender of Sizhou in name.

units.zh: 漢祖起義於河東，以崇為特進、檢校太尉、行太原尹。
units.en: When the Han founder rose in Hedong, Chong was made Special Grand Master, acting Grand Guardian, and acting Prefect of Taiyuan.
units.literal: When the Han founder raised the righteous army in Hedong, Chong was made Special Grand Master, acting Grand Guardian, and acting Prefect of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 是歲五月，漢祖南行，以崇為北京留守，尋加同平章事。
units.en: That fifth month, when the Han founder marched south, Chong was left regent of the northern capital and soon made Grand Councilor.
units.literal: That year in the fifth month, when the Han founder marched south, Chong was made northern capital regent; soon he was also made Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 隱帝嗣位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。
units.en: When Emperor Yindi succeeded, Chong was made acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When Emperor Yindi succeeded, Chong was further made acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 乾祐二年九月，加兼中書令。
units.en: In the ninth month of Qianyou's second year he was also made Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Qianyou he was further made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 時漢隱帝以幼年在位，政在大臣，崇亦招募亡命，繕完兵甲，為自全之計，朝廷命令，多不稟行，征斂一方，略無虛日，人甚苦之。
units.en: Emperor Yindi was young and power lay with ministers. Chong recruited fugitives, armed himself for safety, ignored many court orders, and taxed his region without respite until the people groaned.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Yindi of Han was young on the throne and government lay with the great ministers. Chong also recruited fugitives, repaired armor and weapons as a plan for self-preservation, and often did not obey court orders. He levied on his region day after day without pause, and the people suffered greatly.

units.zh: 三年十一月，隱帝遇害，朝廷議立崇之子徐州節度使赟為主，會周太祖為軍眾所推，降封赟為湘陰公。
units.en: In the eleventh month of the third year Yindi was murdered. The court considered Chong's son Yun of Xuzhou, but the Zhou founder was raised by the army and Yun was reduced to Duke of Xiangyin.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year Emperor Yindi was murdered. The court deliberated installing Chong's son Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, as ruler, but the Zhou founder was pushed by the army; Yun was demoted to Duke of Xiangyin.

units.zh: 崇乃遣牙將李筠奉書求赟歸藩，會赟已死，唯以優辭答之。
units.en: Chong sent Li Yun to beg Yun's return; when Yun was already dead he answered with gracious words only.
